CONFIRM C0173 | Premise: `EvidenceStore.verify_bundle()` iterates `zip(bundle.records, bundle.inclusion_proofs)`, checks optional `chain_hash` equality, then calls `self._chain.verify_inclusion_proof(proof, bundle.merkle_root)`. Concrete trace: if `bundle.records[0]` is replaced with an unrelated raw record that has the same `chain_hash` field copied from the original proof target, proof verification still succeeds because the verifier never recomputes or compares the record’s sealed-body-derived hash; it trusts `proof["chain_hash"]`. Consequence: exported bundles can contain misleading record content while still verifying. This is a HARD correctness constraint and the finding is CONFIRMED. Falsifier: if verification recomputed the record hash from `record["sealed_body"]`/hash fields and rejected mismatches, claim would fail. Attempt: traced code path; no such recomputation exists. Result: claim holds.

EXTEND C0173 | Additional downstream consequence: this is not limited to maliciously edited bundles after export. Any serialization/transport bug that mutates `record["sealed_body"]` but leaves top-level `chain_hash` intact will still yield `verify_bundle(...)=True`, so external auditors can accept corrupted evidence content as authentic. Simplest sufficient fix remains: recompute expected `entry_hash` and `chain_hash` from the bundled record and compare to both `record["chain_hash"]` and `proof["chain_hash"]` before inclusion-proof verification.

CONFIRM C0165 | Premise: `verify_bundle()` accepts any `bundle.merkle_root` and validates proofs against it, but never checks whether that root corresponds to an epoch published by the source chain or to `bundle.chain_metadata`. Concrete trace: create bundle with valid records/proofs from this chain, set `bundle.merkle_root` to the current full-chain root embedded in each proof; verification passes even if that root was never sealed as a published epoch. Consequence: “verifiable against a published epoch root” contract is not met; auditors can be told a bundle is valid without any anchoring to an actually published epoch. HARD interface/correctness constraint, CONFIRMED. Falsifier: if method checked `bundle.merkle_root` against `self._chain.epochs[*]["merkle_root"]` or equivalent bundle field, claim would fail. Attempt: traced method; no epoch-membership check exists. Result: claim holds.

EXTEND C0162 | Premise: `export_bundle()` accepts multiple selectors (`finding_id`, `model`, `round_idx`, `experiment`) but when `record_indices is None` it passes all non-None filters into `_index.search()`, which is strict AND logic. The docstring says “Specify records by index, or by entity filter” and each named selector is phrased independently as “Include all records ...”, which implies union-style convenience for export use. Concrete trace: `export_bundle(model="Gemini", round_idx=5)` returns only Gemini round-5 records, not all Gemini records plus all round-5 records. Consequence: caller can silently export an incomplete bundle and believe multiple requested scopes were included. This is an interface/documentation mismatch; likely already captured. HARD/SOFT split: behavior itself is valid, contract wording is ambiguous; classify SOFT interface defect, CONFIRMED. Falsifier: if surrounding API docs explicitly stated filters are AND-combined for bundle export, this would be rejected. Attempt: checked `query()` docs explicitly say AND-combined, `export_bundle()` docs do not. Result: scoped claim holds as documentation/interface inconsistency, not core logic bug.

No novel findings survived falsification above consequence threshold beyond the registry items extended/confirmed above. Given γ=0.506 and ρ=0.179, submitting speculative duplicates would be noise. Definitive stance: 2 confirmations, 2 extensions, 0 new discoveries.
